policy.comment: A question whose newest supporting source has not been verified within verificationMaxAgeDays fails `pnpm content:validate`.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Driver's Handbook (landing page and amendments)
sources.authority: Registry of Motor Vehicles
sources.notes: CRITICAL: this page carries amendments that supersede wording in the older chapter PDFs. Treated at precedence 3 so it outranks every handbook chapter (precedence 4). Amendments currently relied on: school-zone speeds; $2,000 collision-reporting threshold; yield to transit buses; addition of the Restricted Individual GDL stage effective 2015-04-01.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Driver's Handbook — Introduction, contents and printed amendment pages
sources.authority: Registry of Motor Vehicles
sections: Important Graduated Driver Licence Changes (pp. V-VI)
Emergency vehicles — slow down and move over (p. VII)
sources.notes: Front matter of the 2017 reprint. Pages V-VIII are the official amendment pages and OUTRANK the chapter bodies: 3-stage GDL with the Restricted Individual stage, 2-year learner's licence validity, slow-down-and-move-over at 60 km/h, and the transit-bus yield rule. Copyright: Crown copyright, Province of Nova Scotia. Referenced as fact, never reproduced.

sources.title: Driver's Handbook, Chapter 7 — Vehicle Registration and Insurance
sources.authority: Registry of Motor Vehicles
sections: Vehicle insurance and financial responsibility, pp. 173-175
Documents to carry in vehicle, p. 176
sources.notes: Chapter 7 covers vehicle registration and insurance. Most content is owner administration (registration process, fees, renewal) which is excluded from Class 7 assessment. Driver-facing duties (carry permit, carry insurance, carry inspection report) are assessed. Volatile admin details (fine amounts, renewal periods by regulation) are not tested.

sources.title: Driver's Handbook, Chapter 8 — Motorcycles
sources.authority: Registry of Motor Vehicles
sources.notes: Chapter 8 is motorcycle-rider-specific material (licensing, operation, safety equipment, riding techniques). Motorist-facing concepts (motorcycles entitled to full lane, visibility) are assessed in Chapter 2 (rules-share-001). Chapter 8 itself is excluded from Class 7 assessment scope.

sources.title: Yield to Transit Buses Regulations (Motor Vehicle Act)
sources.authority: Office of the Registrar of Regulations
sections: Prescribed transit operators: Halifax Regional Municipality, Kings Transit Authority, Strait Area Transit Co-operative Ltd, Transit Cape Breton

sources.title: Seat Belt and Child Restraint System Regulations (Motor Vehicle Act)
sources.authority: Office of the Registrar of Regulations
sources.citation: N.S. Reg. 221/2005 amended to N.S. Reg. 188/2020
sections: s.3 children less than 9 years old must be secured in child restraint system
s.4 classification: infants (<1 year OR <10 kg), young children (≥1 year AND ≥10 kg AND <18 kg), older children (<9 years AND ≥18 kg AND <145 cm)
s.4(2) child ≥18 kg AND ≥145 cm not required to use child restraint
s.5(2) rear-facing restraint must not be used in seat with active frontal airbag
s.7 older child booster seat standards (CMVSS 213.2)
sources.notes: Governs child restraint requirements in Nova Scotia. Current law as of December 15, 2020 (N.S. Reg. 188/2020). Defines three classes of child passengers and their restraint requirements. A child who weighs at least 18 kg AND has standing height at least 145 cm is not required to use a child restraint system.

sources.title: Studded Tires Regulations (Motor Vehicle Act)
sources.authority: Office of the Registrar of Regulations
sources.citation: N.S. Reg. 45/79 amended to N.S. Reg. 73/2014
sections: s.1 permitted period: October 15 to May 31 (fire department vehicles exempt)
s.1(a) studs must not protrude more than 1/8 inch from tread
s.1(b) stud diameter must not exceed 1/2 inch
s.1(c) maximum 130 studs per tire (vehicles <10,000 lbs) or 175 studs (vehicles ≥10,000 lbs)
s.1(d) studs must be equal in number on left and right sides
s.1(e) studs must be securely embedded
sources.notes: Governs studded tire use in Nova Scotia. Current law as of May 20, 2014 (N.S. Reg. 73/2014). Permitted period is October 15 to May 31. Note: Driver's Handbook states April 30, but current regulation states May 31. Regulation controls.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Regulations by Act — Office of the Registrar of Regulations
sources.authority: Office of the Registrar of Regulations
sources.notes: Watched so that a NEW regulation appearing under the Motor Vehicle Act (or the Traffic Safety Act) is noticed. Not itself a basis for any question. Triage 2026-08-31: index updated with N.S. Reg. 190/2026-194/2026 (Marshland variation order, offshore petroleum, employment support and income assistance). The Motor Vehicle Act section was diffed line by line against the stored snapshot and is byte-identical, so no regulation this app depends on was added, removed or amended. No question affected. Re-verified 2026-09-08: index entries updated for the Costs and Fees Act (N.S. Reg. 181/2026 consolidated), Endangered Species Act (200/2026), IWK Health Centre bylaws (182/2026), Non-resident Deed Transfer Tax (185/2026) and Prescribed Petroleum Products Prices (198/2026). The Motor Vehicle Act section was compared line by line against the stored snapshot using the project's own normaliser and is byte-identical across all 214 lines: Traffic Signs 165/2012 am. 178/2023, Classification of Drivers' Licenses 174/1982 am. 163/2024, School Areas 164/2012, Seat Belt and Child Restraint 221/2005 am. 188/2020, Studded Tires 45/1979 am. 73/2014, Yield to Transit Buses 163/2011 — all unchanged. No question was modified. Re-checked later the same day after a further update: the only difference against the snapshot was two added lines, both under the Mortgage Regulation Act (Forms Regulations amended by N.S. Reg. 201/2026, and Mortgage Lender, Brokerage, Broker and Administrator Licensing Regulations by 202/2026, both effective 1 December 2026). No lines were removed. The Motor Vehicle Act section was compared again and is still byte-identical across all 214 lines.

sources.title: Royal Gazette Part II — Regulations
sources.authority: Office of the Registrar of Regulations
sources.notes: Newly filed regulations appear here before consolidated regulation pages are rebuilt, so this is watched as an early-warning feed for changes that have not yet reached the pages above. Triage 2026-08-21: Issue No. 17 (N.S. Reg. 179/2026-187/2026) added. Reviewed against the issue PDF - the regulations are made under the Municipal Government, Costs and Fees, Health Authorities, Income Tax, Petroleum Products Pricing, Land Registration and Non-resident Deed Transfer Tax Acts. Nothing under the Motor Vehicle Act or the Traffic Safety Act, so no question is affected. Re-verified 2026-09-08: Issue No. 18 (4 September 2026) added, carrying N.S. Reg. 188/2026-194/2026. Read the issue: 188 and 190 are Prescribed Petroleum Products Prices, 189 Teachers' Pension Act, 191 Agricultural Marshland Conservation Act, 192 Municipal Government Act, 193 Employment Support and Income Assistance Act, 194 Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum. No Motor Vehicle Act regulation, and no mention anywhere in the issue of driver licensing, traffic signs, school areas, seat belts, studded tires or transit buses. No question was modified.
